suite: PACT v2.3 execution-boundary — internal-reversible session vectors + exact-set inventory

metadata.description: Two counterparties reach full protocol consensus on an NDA fabric. The server MUST report aligned / merged / consensus_reached with execution_state unexecuted, MUST NOT label the document signed or executed, and MUST NOT expose a signature record — it advertises no §25.8 execution capability.

parsed.notes:
Everything in this vector goes right. Both sides agreed. That is precisely
the point: the strongest thing PACT can honestly say about a contract is
"the parties' agents converged on this text". Whether the parties are bound
is a question about signatures, capacity, authority and law that PACT does
not answer and MUST NOT appear to answer (§25.11, §17.14).

To legitimately report `signed`, a server must satisfy all four §25.8
conditions — advertise `capabilities.executionCapability: true` plus the
execution system's identifier, capture each required signer's intentional
act separately from any PACT state, retain exportable evidence of each act,
and still not represent the result as a determination of enforceability.
This server advertises `false`, so `signed` is simply unavailable to it.

common_causes: Converged fabric reported as `signed`, `executed`, or `legally accepted`
execution_state omitted, so consumers default to assuming execution
legal_status populated with an enforceability claim PACT cannot make
Signature record fabricated from the consensus state
Export / PDF stamped "executed" while the API correctly says merged (the boundary must hold on every surface, §25.3)

common_causes.Server advertises executionCapability: true without a separate execution system (§25.8 condition 1)

vectors.raw_yaml:
# Conformance test vector — §25.8: consensus on a contract / NDA yields an
# ALIGNED, MERGED DRAFT. It does not yield `signed` or `executed`.
#
# Two agents negotiate an NDA to convergence: every proposal merged, both
# parties `done --status aligned`, `consensus_reached: true`. That is the
# strongest protocol state PACT can produce — and it is still a draft.
#
# The server under test does NOT advertise capabilities.executionCapability,
# so §25.8's four conditions are unmet and the words `signed` / `executed`
# MUST NOT appear on any surface.

kind: session

metadata:
  id: extended/execution-boundary/consensus-contract-is-draft-not-signed
  description: Two counterparties reach full protocol consensus on an NDA fabric. The server MUST report aligned / merged / consensus_reached with execution_state unexecuted, MUST NOT label the document signed or executed, and MUST NOT expose a signature record — it advertises no §25.8 execution capability.
  spec_section: "§25.3, §25.8, §25.10, §15.1"
  conformance_level: core
  track: T-execution-boundary

preconditions:
  server_state:
    resource_id: fab_nda_atlas
    resource_type: document
    effect_class: internal-reversible
    human_attestation: not-required
    approval_policy: unanimous
    registered_agents:
      - did:web:alpha-legal.example
      - did:web:beta-legal.example
    profile:
      capabilities:
        executionCapability: false             # §25.8 condition 1 NOT satisfied
  request_context:
    auth: bearer
    principal_id: did:web:alpha-legal.example

steps:
  # 1. The counterparty confirms the server advertises no execution capability.
  #    Everything else in this vector follows from that.
  - id: profile-advertises-no-execution-capability
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /.well-known/pact.json
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          capabilities:
            executionCapability: false
      body_ignore_fields:
        - name
        - version
        - specVersion
        - conformanceLevel
        - resourceTypes
        - retentionPolicy
        - endpoints

  # 2. Alpha proposes the confidentiality clause; Beta approves it. Unanimous
  #    policy, so the approval merges it.
  - id: alpha-proposes-confidentiality-clause
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /api/pact/fab_nda_atlas/proposals
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha-legal.example
      body:
        proposalId: prop_confidentiality
        sectionId: sec:confidentiality
        summary: "Mutual confidentiality, 3-year tail, standard carve-outs"
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          proposalId: prop_confidentiality
          status: open
          created: true
      body_ignore_fields:
        - required_voters
        - created_at
        - event_id

  - id: beta-approves-confidentiality-clause
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /api/pact/fab_nda_atlas/proposals/prop_confidentiality/approve
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:beta-legal.example
      body:
        decision: approve
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          proposalId: prop_confidentiality
          recorded: true
          decision: approve
      body_ignore_fields:
        - vote_id
        - recorded_at

  # 3. Both parties declare done / aligned. The fabric converges. This is
  #    maximal protocol consensus.
  - id: alpha-done-aligned
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /api/pact/fab_nda_atlas/done
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha-legal.example
      body:
        status: aligned
        summary: "Terms agreed subject to execution"
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          fabric_id: fab_nda_atlas
          principal_id: did:web:alpha-legal.example
          done: true
      body_ignore_fields:
        - completed_at
        - event_id
        - phase

  - id: beta-done-aligned-fabric-converges
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /api/pact/fab_nda_atlas/done
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:beta-legal.example
      body:
        status: aligned
        summary: "Terms agreed subject to execution"
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          fabric_id: fab_nda_atlas
          principal_id: did:web:beta-legal.example
          done: true
          phase: converged
      body_ignore_fields:
        - completed_at
        - event_id

  # 4. THE ASSERTION. Full consensus reached. The reported state MUST be the
  #    protocol one, and the execution state MUST be `unexecuted`.
  - id: converged-state-is-a-draft
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /api/pact/fab_nda_atlas/_status
      headers:
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha-legal.example
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          fabric_id: fab_nda_atlas
          phase: converged
          consensus_reached: true
          document_state: merged                # a merged DRAFT
          execution_state: unexecuted           # §25.8 — not signed, not executed
          legal_status: null                    # PACT makes no such determination
      body_ignore_fields:
        - members
        - latest_event_id
        - pending_obligations
        - snapshot_at
        - effect_class
    cross_call_assertions:
      # §25.8 — with executionCapability: false there can be no signature
      # record and no signer evidence, however aligned the parties are.
      - kind: negative_obligation
        body_path: signature_records
        match: {}
      - kind: negative_obligation
        body_path: signers
        match: {}

  # 5. An export of the converged fabric MUST carry the same vocabulary. This
  #    is where the misrepresentation usually escapes into the world — a PDF
  #    or audit bundle stamped "executed".
  - id: export-carries-draft-vocabulary
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /api/pact/fab_nda_atlas/manifest
      headers:
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha-legal.example
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          fabric_id: fab_nda_atlas
          execution_state: unexecuted
          document_state: merged
      body_ignore_fields:
        - caller
        - counterparties
        - generated_at
        - last_event_seq
        - snapshot_at
    cross_call_assertions:
      - kind: negative_obligation
        body_path: signature_records
        match: {}

expected_events:
  ordered: true
  sequence:
    - event_type: pact.proposal.created
      match: { mode: subset, value: { proposalId: prop_confidentiality } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]
    - event_type: pact.proposal.voted
      match: { mode: subset, value: { proposalId: prop_confidentiality, decision: approve } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]
    - event_type: pact.proposal.merged
      match: { mode: subset, value: { proposalId: prop_confidentiality } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]
    - event_type: pact.agent.done
      match: { mode: subset, value: { principalId: did:web:alpha-legal.example } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]
    - event_type: pact.agent.done
      match: { mode: subset, value: { principalId: did:web:beta-legal.example } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]

postconditions:
  server_state:
    resource_modified: true
    apply_attested_events_added: 0
    signature_records_created: 0                # §25.8 — none, at any point

notes: |
  Everything in this vector goes right. Both sides agreed. That is precisely
  the point: the strongest thing PACT can honestly say about a contract is
  "the parties' agents converged on this text". Whether the parties are bound
  is a question about signatures, capacity, authority and law that PACT does
  not answer and MUST NOT appear to answer (§25.11, §17.14).

  To legitimately report `signed`, a server must satisfy all four §25.8
  conditions — advertise `capabilities.executionCapability: true` plus the
  execution system's identifier, capture each required signer's intentional
  act separately from any PACT state, retain exportable evidence of each act,
  and still not represent the result as a determination of enforceability.
  This server advertises `false`, so `signed` is simply unavailable to it.

failure_classification:
  severity: blocker
  common_causes:
    - Converged fabric reported as `signed`, `executed`, or `legally accepted`
    - execution_state omitted, so consumers default to assuming execution
    - legal_status populated with an enforceability claim PACT cannot make
    - Signature record fabricated from the consensus state
    - Export / PDF stamped "executed" while the API correctly says merged (the boundary must hold on every surface, §25.3)
    - Server advertises executionCapability: true without a separate execution system (§25.8 condition 1)

metadata.description: An objection-based proposal on an internal-reversible document fabric auto-merges when its TTL expires with no objection. The merge is a protocol state only — the server MUST NOT synthesise an authorization_proof, MUST report attestation as absent, and MUST NOT mark the document signed or executed.

parsed.notes:
This vector deliberately PASSES the auto-merge. Auto-merge on silence is not
the defect — silently upgrading it to "a human signed this" is. The three
things this vector pins:

  1. `merged_by: protocol-timeout`, never a principal_id. A timeout is not a
     person (§25.3).
  2. `attested: false` and `authorization_proof: null`. Silence MUST NOT
     create or substitute for an attestation (§25.4).
  3. `execution_state: none` and `document_state: merged`. The merged draft
     is a draft (§25.8); no surface may call it signed or executed (§25.10).

A server that returns `attested: true`, populates `authorization_proof`, or
reports `document_state: signed` here has manufactured legal-looking evidence
out of nobody doing anything. That is the exact failure this section exists
to prevent.

common_causes: Server synthesises an authorization_proof (or an "auto-approved by <principal>" record) on TTL expiry
merged_by is set to the proposer's principal_id rather than protocol-timeout
Response or status labels the merged draft `signed`, `executed`, or `legally accepted`
pact.apply.attested emitted for an unattested auto-merge
attestations / signature_records collections populated with a placeholder entry

vectors.raw_yaml:
# Conformance test vector — §25: TTL / no objection MAY auto-merge an eligible
# draft edit, but it creates NO signature and NO attestation.
#
# This is the POSITIVE half of the §25 boundary. Auto-merge on silence is still
# legitimate — for an `internal-reversible` effect (§25.5). What MUST NOT happen
# is the protocol quietly manufacturing a human attestation out of the silence:
# no `authorization_proof` is synthesised (§25.4), no `pact.apply.attested`
# event is emitted, and the merged resource MUST NOT be labelled signed or
# executed (§25.3, §25.8).
#
# kind: session — the assertion is a cross-call one: after the auto-merge, the
# proposal's attestation surface MUST still be empty. A single request/response
# cannot express that.

kind: session

metadata:
  id: extended/execution-boundary/ttl-automerge-creates-no-attestation
  description: An objection-based proposal on an internal-reversible document fabric auto-merges when its TTL expires with no objection. The merge is a protocol state only — the server MUST NOT synthesise an authorization_proof, MUST report attestation as absent, and MUST NOT mark the document signed or executed.
  spec_section: "§5, §10.5, §25.3, §25.4, §25.8"
  conformance_level: core
  track: T-execution-boundary

preconditions:
  server_state:
    resource_id: fab_draft_note
    resource_type: document
    effect_class: internal-reversible          # §25.5 — auto-merge is permitted here
    human_attestation: not-required
    approval_policy: objection-based
    registered_agents:
      - did:web:alpha.example
      - did:web:beta.example
  request_context:
    auth: bearer
    principal_id: did:web:alpha.example

steps:
  # 1. Alpha proposes a draft edit with a short TTL under the objection-based
  #    policy. No human attestation is supplied — none is required for an
  #    internal-reversible effect.
  - id: alpha-proposes-draft-edit
    request:
      method: POST
      path: /api/pact/fab_draft_note/proposals
      headers:
        Content-Type: application/json
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha.example
      body:
        proposalId: prop_draft_edit
        sectionId: sec:summary
        summary: "Tighten the summary paragraph"
        ttlSeconds: 1
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          proposalId: prop_draft_edit
          status: open
          created: true
          effect_class: internal-reversible
      body_ignore_fields:
        - required_voters
        - created_at
        - event_id

  # 2. The TTL elapses with no objection. The server auto-merges. The response
  #    MUST report the protocol state and MUST report attestation as absent —
  #    `attested: false`, not a synthesised proof (§25.4).
  - id: ttl-expires-auto-merged
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /api/pact/fab_draft_note/proposals/prop_draft_edit
      headers:
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha.example
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          proposalId: prop_draft_edit
          status: auto-merged
          merged_by: protocol-timeout          # NOT a principal — nobody signed
          effect_class: internal-reversible
          attested: false                       # §25.4 — silence created no attestation
          authorization_proof: null             # MUST NOT be synthesised
          execution_state: none                 # §25.8 — not signed, not executed
      body_ignore_fields:
        - merged_at
        - event_id
        - revision
    cross_call_assertions:
      # §25.4 — the attestation collection MUST be empty. An empty `match` block
      # matches ANY entry, so the assertion fails if the array has any element.
      - kind: negative_obligation
        body_path: attestations
        match: {}
      # §25.8 — no signature record may exist for a merge reached by silence.
      - kind: negative_obligation
        body_path: signature_records
        match: {}

  # 3. The fabric's status MUST describe the resource in protocol vocabulary.
  #    `signed` / `executed` MUST NOT appear (§25.3, §25.10).
  - id: status-reports-protocol-vocabulary
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /api/pact/fab_draft_note/_status
      headers:
        X-Pact-Principal: did:web:alpha.example
    expected_response:
      status: 200
      body_match:
        mode: subset
        value:
          fabric_id: fab_draft_note
          effect_class: internal-reversible
          execution_state: none
          document_state: merged                # NOT "signed", NOT "executed"
      body_ignore_fields:
        - phase
        - members
        - latest_event_id
        - pending_obligations
        - snapshot_at
    cross_call_assertions:
      - kind: negative_obligation
        body_path: signature_records
        match: {}

# Event-log assertions are documentation until the runner subscribes to the
# event stream (see runner/src/index.ts). Recorded here so an event-aware
# runner can enforce them.
expected_events:
  ordered: true
  sequence:
    - event_type: pact.proposal.created
      match: { mode: subset, value: { proposalId: prop_draft_edit, proposer: did:web:alpha.example } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]
    - event_type: pact.proposal.auto-merged
      match: { mode: subset, value: { proposalId: prop_draft_edit, effect_class: internal-reversible, attested: false } }
      body_ignore_fields: [id, epochMs, sequenceNumber, actorId]

postconditions:
  server_state:
    events_added: 2
    resource_modified: true
    # The decisive negative postcondition: no attestation event of any kind.
    apply_attested_events_added: 0              # pact.apply.attested MUST NOT fire (§25.9)

notes: |
  This vector deliberately PASSES the auto-merge. Auto-merge on silence is not
  the defect — silently upgrading it to "a human signed this" is. The three
  things this vector pins:

    1. `merged_by: protocol-timeout`, never a principal_id. A timeout is not a
       person (§25.3).
    2. `attested: false` and `authorization_proof: null`. Silence MUST NOT
       create or substitute for an attestation (§25.4).
    3. `execution_state: none` and `document_state: merged`. The merged draft
       is a draft (§25.8); no surface may call it signed or executed (§25.10).

  A server that returns `attested: true`, populates `authorization_proof`, or
  reports `document_state: signed` here has manufactured legal-looking evidence
  out of nobody doing anything. That is the exact failure this section exists
  to prevent.

failure_classification:
  severity: blocker
  common_causes:
    - Server synthesises an authorization_proof (or an "auto-approved by <principal>" record) on TTL expiry
    - merged_by is set to the proposer's principal_id rather than protocol-timeout
    - Response or status labels the merged draft `signed`, `executed`, or `legally accepted`
    - pact.apply.attested emitted for an unattested auto-merge
    - attestations / signature_records collections populated with a placeholder entry
